note: Lead hook, rebuilt (step 4). The old one reached the head with the arm three-quarters straight and travelling forward: it read as a jab with a turn on it. A hook is a bent arm swung round by the body: a small load onto the lead side, then the lead heel turns out and the hips and shoulders come round together, the elbow lifts level with the fist and stays bent at about a right angle, so the fist comes in from OUTSIDE his guard and travels across, not forward. Rear hand on the chin, chin tucked behind the lead shoulder, and through a little past the target before it comes home. Reach 0.66 of the arm: the body closes the rest (far), so the arm keeps its shape.

keys.note: the load: weight onto the lead leg, a small turn the other way, the lead hand opening out from the face
the swing begins: the elbow up level with the shoulder, the fist out wide of his guard
impact: hips and shoulders round, lead heel turned out, the fist come across onto the jaw with the elbow still up
through it: a hand's width past the target before it comes back
